content.title: Reach the frozen-user banking overview with transfers unavailable
content.intent: Prove that frozen_user reaches any permitted authenticated banking overview state while transfer functionality is unavailable, disabled, or rejected through normal UI paths.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the documented persona fixture frozen_user because persona changes the outcome; applied auth/permission because the promise is post-login and role/state gated; applied negative/error because the key behavior is blocked transfer access. Risk gate implied strength=3 because money and auth apply, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because this path is defined by a single persona class.

content.title: Standard-user dashboard does not expose administrative-only capabilities
content.intent: Prove that a standard_user banking experience does not surface administrative-only capabilities or data.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to standard_user versus admin_user persona outcomes; applied auth/permission because the distinction is role-based; applied negative/error because the path proves forbidden access is not available to a non-admin. Risk gate implied strength=3 because auth applies, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because the persona alone determines the outcome class.

content.title: Reach a distinct administrative banking dashboard as admin_user
content.intent: Prove that admin_user lands in the intended administrative experience and that it is distinguishable from the ordinary customer-facing dashboard.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the documented admin_user persona; applied auth/permission because the dashboard is role-aware after authentication; applied state/flow because the path starts at successful login and ends in the authenticated destination view. Risk gate implied strength=3 because auth applies, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because the persona is the single outcome-changing input.

content.title: Show a consistent negative balance for overdraft_user
content.intent: Prove that overdraft_user sees a negative balance and that the balance reconciles with the related account and transaction information.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the overdraft_user persona because it represents a distinct negative-balance state; applied state/flow because the path spans dashboard to related banking views; applied currency/money-state reasoning because financial values must stay consistent across views. Risk gate implied strength=3 because money applies, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because the persona state itself defines the edge case.

content.title: Expose the wrong loan total for error_user in a reachable banking view
content.intent: Prove that error_user reaches a dashboard/admin/navigation path with loan information, shows the documented wrong-loan-total condition, and keeps that state distinguishable from generic failure.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the documented error_user persona because it represents a distinct wrong-loan-total outcome class; applied state/flow because the path may require navigation from the landing view to the first reachable loan-related banking view; applied negative/error because the state must remain distinguishable from generic failure. Risk gate implied strength=3 because money applies, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because this path is driven by the persona class and reachable loan surface.

content.title: Reach the standard-user banking overview with persona, accounts, balances, and transaction visibility
content.intent: Prove that a successful standard_user login lands on the authenticated banking overview and exposes or links to the relevant banking state for that persona.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the standard_user persona as the baseline full-access class; applied auth/permission because the scenario begins with successful authentication; applied state/flow because the path covers landing plus access to dashboard-linked banking information. Risk gate implied strength=3 because money and auth apply, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because persona is the only outcome-changing class in this baseline path.

content.title: Show loading progress and resolve consistently for slow_user
content.intent: Prove that slow_user sees understandable loading or progress feedback and eventually reaches a consistent authenticated banking experience.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the documented slow_user persona because it represents intentionally slow-loading behavior; applied state/flow because the scenario must traverse a loading state into the resolved dashboard; applied negative/error reasoning to ensure the surface does not appear permanently broken. Risk gate implied strength=3 because the resolved state contains money-facing information, but no combinatorial input matrix was needed because the persona class alone defines this path.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied equivalence partitioning because the source defines discrete persona fixtures�standard, admin, frozen, overdraft, slow, and error�with outcome-changing dashboard behavior.
[applicability] Applied auth/permission because the dashboard is explicitly the authenticated banking overview and several promises depend on role or persona-gated access.
[applicability] Applied state/flow because every path begins with successful login and several journeys continue through navigation or loading into a resolved banking state.
[applicability] Applied negative/error techniques to frozen_user and standard_user non-admin coverage because the source makes forbidden or rejected behavior part of the intended product experience.

[applicability] Did not apply boundary value analysis because the source for this use-case does not define an ordered numeric, date, or length-bounded dashboard input whose boundaries change dashboard outcomes.

[applicability] Did not mint a dashboard accessibility scenario because the cited dashboard source text states no dashboard-specific accessibility promise; existing login accessibility coverage is a reuse candidate for a different use-case.
[applicability] Did not mint an i18n scenario because the cited dashboard and persona source text does not promise locale-specific dashboard formatting or translation behavior.

[applicability] Did not mint list/pagination scenarios because the source promises visibility or accessibility of accounts and transactions, but does not specify dashboard sorting, filtering, or page-size behavior.
